/-!
# Erdős Problem 728

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/728](https://www.erdosproblems.com/728)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Real
open scoped Nat Topology

namespace Erdos728

/--
Let $\varepsilon$ be sufficiently small and $C, C' > 0$. Are there integers $a, b, n$ such that
$$a, b > \varepsilon n\quad a!\, b! \mid n!\, (a + b - n)!, $$
and
$$C \log n < a + b - n < C' \log n ?$$

Note that the website currently displays a simpler (trivial) version of this problem because
$a + b$ isn't assumed to be in the $n + O(\log n)$ regime.

Barreto and ChatGPT-5.2 have proved that, for any $0 < C_1 < C_2$, there are infinitely many
$a, b, n$ with $b = n/2$, $a = n/2 + O(\log n)$, and $C_1 \log n < a + b - n < C_2 \log n$ such
that $a! b! \mid n! (a + b - n)!$

This appears to answer the question in the spirit it was intended.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos728p.lean"]
theorem erdos_728 :
    answer(True) ↔
      ∀ᶠ ε : ℝ in 𝓝[>] 0, ∀ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ C' > C,
        ∃ a b n : ℕ,
          0 < n ∧
          ε * n < a ∧
          ε * n < b ∧
          a ! * b ! ∣ n ! * (a + b - n)! ∧
          a + b > n + C * log n ∧
          a + b < n + C' * log n := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): Use Legendre's formula to test divisibility in terms of p-adic valuations.

end Erdos728

findings.description: The opening sentence of the docstring (line 34) assumes only `C, C' > 0`, whereas the Lean statement correctly requires `0 < C < C'`. Read literally, the prose includes choices such as C = C', for which the two strict logarithmic bounds are incompatible. The following paragraph already gives the correct ordering, so this is only a prose omission; the Lean mathematics is correct.
findings.source_evidence: Sothanaphan, “Resolution of Erdős Problem #728,” arXiv:2601.07421v4, Theorem 1 (“Logarithmic gap window”), begins “Fix 0<C₁<C₂” and concludes C₁ log n < a+b−n < C₂ log n. Read in the LaTeX source at https://arxiv.org/e-print/2601.07421v4.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the opening sentence to assume `0 < C < C'` rather than merely `C, C' > 0`.

reformulations.difference: Lean requests one triple for each logarithmic window, while the discussed solution describes infinitely many triples. An explicit infinitude quantifier is unnecessary for the window formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Fix ε satisfying the universally quantified window property. Every witness has n>1, so r=(a+b−n)/log n is defined with positive denominator. If some window (C,C') contained only finitely many admissible triples, their finitely many r-values could be avoided by a smaller nonempty window inside (C,C'). Applying the same existence property to that smaller window gives a contradiction. Conversely, infinitely many triples imply existence. The full equivalence obtained by replacing the existential triples in this theorem's right-hand side with an infinite set was proved in `/workspace/review/equivalences.lean` as `Review728.main_infinite_equiv`, without using the theorem under review.

review.notes:
No mathematical misformalization or status issue was found. The logarithmic-window interpretation is explicitly distinguished from the loose original wording and is supported by Sothanaphan's result. Lean checks confirmed the nonvacuous meaning of sufficiently small positive ε, exclusion of n=0 and n=1, and positivity of a+b−n, so natural subtraction does not alter the factorial condition. Small factorial cases and a complete small witness were also tested.

The linked proof's density-one binomial-divisibility result with k≤exp(0.5√log m) implies the stated logarithmic windows by taking n=2m, b=m, and a=m+k. Its relevant definitions and conclusions were inspected; no active `sorry` or custom axioms were found. It was not recompiled under its original Lean version. The independent equivalence proofs compiled successfully and use only standard axioms.

The live erdosproblems.com page and forum returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers. Consequently, the docstring's assertion about the website's current presentation could not be checked directly. The original paper, subsequent mathematical papers, and current independent database were available; the latter records problem 728 as proved (Lean).
